text:
sarah: heads-up — after the OFED + EFA driver rollout to us-east-2 this morning I'm seeing a consistent NCCL bandwidth regression on a subset of GPU hosts. initial tracing points to SRQ (shared receive queue) queue starvation patterns. filing here so infra is aware.

matt: confirmed. nccl-allreduce perf down ~60% on euc2a-rack3 nodes. iperf3 between hosts looks fine (~9Gbps), but `ib_read_bw` and `perf query` show long tails and many retries on SRQ completions. not all AZs affected.

infra-bot: deploy job #457 applied OFED 5.3.0 + efa-driver 1.12.0 to cluster euc2a (canary) at 06:12 UTC.

anita: ran quick nccl-tests and captured outputs:
```
# nccl-tests allreduce
bytes  count  alg   busbw  time  errors
...  1024   1    1.2GB/s  ... (degraded)
```
Also `ethtool -S mlx5_core` shows SRQ drops and `mlx5_qlog` indicating queue affinity thrash. attaching inline logs in thread.

jason: can we roll back the OFED patch? last full safe rollout was OFED 5.2.1. rollback will impact clusters with reserved capacity, ops will need SRE coverage.

ops-oncall: short-term mitigation tested on one canary host: disabled SRQ at the driver level and perf returned to baseline for nccl tests. commands used: `echo 0 > /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/device/srq_enable` (host path varies), then `systemctl restart efa`. note: disabling SRQ increases CPU/doorbell overhead, need to validate at scale.

matt: disabling SRQ on 1 node brought allreduce back to ~95% of baseline, CPU went +6% on the host. this is acceptable as a stopgap for critical jobs but not ideal long term.

anita: opened ticket with Mellanox/driver vendor, provided pcap-ish logs and `ibstat` dumps. they asked for a kernel dmesg with `MLX5` debug enabled and suggested it might be an SRQ affinity regression introduced by OFED 5.3.0 when combined with new firmware 20.34.

sarah: proposed plan: 1) rollback OFED 5.3.0 on the canary rack tonight (low-traffic window) and validate nccl tests; 2) if rollback fixes, hold rollout and convert affected hosts to patched-but-disabled-SRQ pool; 3) vendor escalation + patch; 4) instrument alert: >25% drop in per-route nccl throughput alerts on the console. any objections?

jason: +1 on rollback canary. coordinate with sales/support for any impacted reserved clusters.

ops-oncall: will script SRQ-disable toggle and a perf-runner that triggers canary checks post-rollback. putting a runbook together now.

matt: also recommend adding a short nccl microbenchmark in the preflight for future OFED/efa rollouts (fail if >15% degradation vs baseline).

anita: will add extra metrics: SRQ completions, mlx5 errors, and nccl tail latency into the console dashboard and link to the runbook.

sarah: thanks all — let's keep this thread as the single source for the incident. I'll update after the rollback test (ETA +3h). :grey_exclamation:
